name: Ned Kelly beard

lead: The Ned Kelly beard takes its name from Ned Kelly, the 19th-century Australian outlaw whose bearded portraits are among the best-known images in Australian history. In grooming discussions it refers to a full, bushy beard look, with a trimmed or shaved upper-lip area in the version described by the wiki's source notes.
A full beard can broaden or add definition to the lower face, which is why men with a softer jawline sometimes choose it. Little has been published about the style under this name.

paras: The look is grown out over several weeks and then shaped at the cheeks and neckline, with the upper-lip area kept short or clean-shaven. Regular trimming and beard oil are common grooming additions.
Facial-hair styling carries no particular health risk beyond skin irritation from shaving or ingrown hairs. Beard density varies by person, which affects how the style fills in.

chain: Grow a full beard and shave the upper-lip area
Beard outlines and extends the jaw and chin
angle.text: A full beard adds visible mass around the jaw and chin and can change perceived face shape; this variant keeps the lip area clear.

lead: The Ned Kelly beard is a facial-hair style named after Ned Kelly (1854-1880), the Australian bushranger known for his homemade armour and for photographs taken in the 1870s and 1880s.[1] It describes a full beard, with the upper-lip region shaved in the version tracked by this wiki.

Men choose full-beard styles to add width and definition to the lower face and to mask a recessed chin or soft jawline. Little published material discusses this particular style, so its description here is limited to its name and general category.

paras: The style is a full beard with the upper lip area shaved, named for Ned Kelly, whose photographs, including a portrait taken in 1880, are widely reproduced.[1]
